messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] calypso-prod-vpc: p99 latency > 3.5s on dedicated pool calypso-pool-3, error rate up, paging #oncall (maria). severity: sev2. links: https://alerts.redwood/2623456789
maria chen: i'm oncall — pulling traces and tailing pod logs. anyone seeing queue depth spikes?
Ajay Patel: i'm here. gpus on node gpu-37 show repeated tiny OOMs and KV cache misses. CPU fallback attempts are spiking. looks like prefix caching thrash from long-chat sessions.
Lee Kim: thanks. can we isolate to calypso tenant-only? confirm if this is tenant-isolated behavior vs pool-wide.
Sophie Rivera: calypso-support on line — customers reporting timeouts in their web UI. can we offer a degradative mitigation while we investigate? they need something low-risk.
Ajay Patel: initial check: failure rate concentrated on calypso-pool-3 backends, 95% traffic from calypso-tenant-id. not cross-tenant.
Nathan O'Neill: ok. options: 1) pin calypso to a safe variant with lower memory profile (safe-variant), 2) route calypso->fallback model (cpu-hosted small) for the bulk of traffic, 3) throttle long-chat sessions via tenant rate limits.
maria chen: priority: reduce customer-visible errors. operationally, i want a quick pin+canary then a communication to calypso. Ajay, can you prepare the pin command? Lee, coordinate the canary policy. Sophie, prep message for customer. Nathan, confirm infra rollback plan if things worsen.
Ajay Patel: running tenant-pin now. snippet:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/calypso/pin \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SRE_TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.2","variant":"safe-0.9","duration_minutes":60}'
```
Ajay Patel: response: 202 accepted. Pin started against calypso-tenant-id -> redwood-1.2:safe-0.9.
Lee Kim: configuring canary rule: 10% traffic -> fallback to redwood-small-safemode (cpu) for 5m, evaluate errors/latency; then 50% if stable. applying route now.
Lee Kim: applied canary: route rule calypso -> fallback redwood-small-safemode 10%.
Sophie Rivera: initial customer message drafted: "We’re investigating elevated inference latency affecting your VPC tenant. As a mitigation we’re routing a small percentage of traffic to a safe fallback and pinning your tenant to a stable model variant to reduce errors. We’ll update you in 15 minutes with status." want me to send?
maria chen: send that now and include expected degraded features: long-chat truncation and slight quality variance. tag eng for followups.
Sophie Rivera: sent to calypso CSM + support@calypso. they acked, asked for ETA.
Nathan O'Neill: monitoring after pin+canary: errors dropped 35% within 2m, p99 down to ~2.1s on pinned hosts but overall pool still noisy. fallback canary 10% shows stable sub-1s on fallback.
Ajay Patel: looks like the safe variant reduced KV working set; memory GC reduced OOMs. next step: if stable for 10m, increase canary to 40% then 100% as planned. also preparing a temporary tenant concurrency cap to limit new long-lived sessions.
maria chen: agree. execute concurrency cap now:
```json
{"tenant_id":"calypso-tenant-id","max_concurrent_sessions":40}
```
Lee Kim: cap applied at the router layer. new session creation 429s expected for heavy usage, existing sessions allowed.
Sophie Rivera: customer responded: "thanks — the UI is improving but we still see occasional 504s on large uploads." asked for a timeline for full restoration.
maria chen: timeline: 30m for full rollback to normal with staged increases, 15m check for canary. i'll call an oncall handoff at +30 if not resolved. Ajay, set a reminder for the 10m checkpoint.
Ajay Patel: reminder set. also opening an infra ticket to repro OOMs in staging with a calypso-like traffic replay: INC-2623456790. tagging eng-runtime.
Lee Kim: note: we should avoid a full model swap in-route unless pinned variant fails. fallback model has lower quality — make sure CSM confirms.
Sophie Rivera: confirmed with CSM: they prefer degraded quality over errors. logging that in customer thread.
maria chen: if canary goes green at +10m, increase to 40%. if any backend OOMs reappear, we revert pin and route 100% to fallback CPU model and escalate to infra (sev1).
Nathan O'Neill: also capturing metrics for postmortem: per-tenant cache hit rate, per-node GPU memory pressure, prefix length distribution, and request concurrency.
Ajay Patel: collecting logs and will paste a short triage in 8m.
incident-bot: [UPDATE] calypso-prod-vpc canary 10% -> fallback reporting success 6m in. error rate down 48%.
maria chen: good. increasing canary to 40% now.
Lee Kim: increased to 40% — monitoring sliding windows.
Sophie Rivera: updated customer: "We’ve increased mitigation and are seeing a drop in errors. We’ll continue to scale mitigations; will follow up in 15 minutes."
Nathan O'Neill: observing p99 on pinned hosts stable ~1.9s; fallback hosts sub-1s but lower quality. no new OOM spikes after pin+cap.
maria chen: planning handoff: i'm oncall for another 25m then handing to Ajay for followthrough and postmortem. Ajay, you ok to pick up?
Ajay Patel: yes — i'll lead postmortem, collect traces, and propose permanent mitigations (cache-tuning + tenant-level long-chat limits vs nicer graceful truncation).
Sophie Rivera: i'll own customer comms and ticket until SLAs closed.
Lee Kim: i'll schedule a quick follow-up with eng-runtime to discuss KV eviction policy and safe-variant memory profile.
maria chen: thanks team. final plan summary: 1) tenant pinned to redwood-1.2:safe-0.9 (60m temporary) 2) concurrency cap applied (40 sessions) 3) staged canary to fallback model (10% -> 40% -> 100% if needed) 4) customer notified and will receive updates every 15m 5) Ajay leads postmortem and eng-runtime action items.
incident-bot: [RESOLVE PROGRESS] incident severity downgraded to sev3; continue monitoring.
